summary: Ember is an open evidence explorer for NASA microgravity combustion data, built for the Flame in Freefall challenge. NASA has studied fire in microgravity for decades, but the results sit in dozens of technical reports. Ember puts them in one place: a map of 643 tests by oxygen and pressure, 255 claims that each cite their report page, and an Ask page that answers only from the evidence or honestly refuses. It shows that 48 tests fall in the planned lunar-base atmosphere (30% oxygen or more at 10.2 psi or less), all in microgravity, and that NASA's PSI archive holds no partial-gravity tests. It also ranks where NASA should test next. This matters because fire is one of the greatest dangers for Moon and Mars habitats, and engineers need cited evidence that also says where the evidence ends. Team of one, with AI assistance.
details:
WHAT IT DOES. Ember is an interactive evidence explorer for NASA's microgravity combustion research. An atmosphere map places every test by oxygen share and pressure and highlights the planned lunar-base air (30% oxygen or more at 10.2 psi or less): 48 tests fall there, all in microgravity. An oxygen dial shows which materials cross their 1 g flammability limits. A Moon safety-margin chart (one NASA paper, three fuels) shows flames burning at lower oxygen at lunar gravity. A ranking shows where NASA should test next, a timeline summarises what a spacecraft fire does (Saffire VI), and an Ask page answers questions with page citations or refuses.

HOW IT WORKS. 24 PSI investigations and NTRS reports were turned into a unified table of 769 tests (643 with both oxygen and pressure), keeping censored outcomes such as externally terminated tests, plus hand-transcribed limit tables with page citations. 255 claims were extracted from 11 NASA reports by one AI model (Gemini) with a quoted span and page, cross-checked by a second model family (a Groq-hosted model), and verified by code gates for the exact quote, numbers and conditions. The reviewer opened and checked each of the 255 claims against its source page. Ask parses conditions such as "30% oxygen at 10.2 psi", matches them to claims and tests, and answers with a citation or refuses. No AI runs when someone asks, so it cannot invent an answer. A coverage grid (340 cells) finds 306 never-tested cells, 51 inside lunar-base air, and ranks them.

IMPACT AND CREATIVITY. Cited fire-safety evidence for Moon and Mars habitats, built around refusal and honest gaps: NASA's PSI archive provides no partial-gravity (Moon or Mars) data, and Ember says so instead of filling the gap. The oxygen dial and the margin chart are warnings, not design values.

TOOLS. Python (data pipeline), plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript (site), GitHub Pages, Gemini and a Groq-hosted model for extraction and cross-checking, Claude for coding help and design. Fonts: Sora and IBM Plex (SIL Open Font License). Code: https://github.com/zainabraza06/Ember
